Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Luminary CTO), Maria (Lead ML Eng), Tanya (Cloud Architect)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Luminary is scoping a 6-8 week POC to validate inference hosting options. Primary success metrics are p95 < 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and throughput to handle 800 QPS peak with graceful degradation. Security requires KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, and a private network option for regulated flows. Redwood AE/SE to run benchmarks and provide cost comparisons for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Next call to review bench marks and security packets.

---
00:00 Alex: okay, uh thanks everyone for joining, i'm alex from redwood, i'm the account lead for this engagement. little bit of agenda, we'll kick off with luminary's goals, go over workload numbers, then priya will talk bench plan and options — hosted, dedicated, private and tradeoffs. sound good?
00:14 Jordan: yep that sounds great, thanks for setting this up. i wanted to make sure we focus on the latency tail and also what happens during our marketing spikes, those are the trick ones..
00:25 Maria: yes the spike pattern is bursty, we can get a 12 minute window where qps jumps 5x, typical avg day is 120 qps, peak is about 800 for 10-15 mins per day. avg prompt length ~220 tokens but many important requests are 32-64 tokens.
00:42 Priya: okay that's really helpful — so the avg tokens are a bit higher but the mission critical ones are short, we'll make sure benchmarks include both 64 and 256 token slices and look at prefix cache effects.
00:54 Tanya: quick security note, some traffic must stay inside our VPC, we have encryption keys in azure keyvault, ideally we want KMS support and ability to bring our own key, plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
01:10 Alex: good call, so from a deployment perspective the decision levers are: latency SLOs, predictable unit cost, and network isolation. typical mapping is: Hosted = fastest to deploy and cheapest short-term; Dedicated = committed capacity with predictable throughput; Private = on-prem/VPC for regulatory requirements. but there are nuance tradeoffs, priya do you want to walk the benchmark plan?
01:30 Priya: sure, i'll outline the plan. step one: baseline synthetic runs mimicking short and long prompt shapes, we'll test 64/256/512 tokens, measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput till GPU saturates. step two: prefix cache scenarios and continuous batching impact. step three: cold-start and warm-hot path with kv-cache retention. we should also do a tails analysis for the marketing spike pattern. i'm thinking 3 runs per scenario to get variance.
02:05 Jordan: how long will that take to run? we have a tight calendar, we'd like results before mid-august.
02:12 Priya: bench runs themselves are quick (hours) but we'll need time to provision test infra and analyze. i can have initial numbers by 2026-08-05, full report by 2026-08-09.
02:25 Maria: one other thing — cost sensitivity: if dedicated requires a 6 month commit we need to see burn examples vs hosted for our bursty pattern. hosted seems cheaper if sporadic but if sustained we want to move to dedicated.
02:40 Alex: yes exactly, and there are also hybrid options where you set a minimum reserved pool and burst on hosted. we can model that in the TCO sheet.
02:52 Tanya: for private deployment, what are the realistic timelines? onboarding with our VPC and KMS, and offline image scans..
03:01 Priya: private (on-prem/VPC) typically adds integration work: network peering, SSO, key management. timeline is more like 6-12 weeks depending on approval paths. dedicated (Redwood Dedicated) sits in the middle — 2-4 weeks for reserved infra and config. hosted is near immediate, like days. but for security review we can run a short pilot in hosted with encrypted payloads to satisfy some auditors.
03:30 Jordan: what's the behavioral difference in latency between hosted and dedicated? do we get better tail on dedicated?
03:38 Priya: yes dedicated reduces noisy neighbor variability, so you often see tighter p95/p99, but depends on the reserved instance size and batching profile. also quantization choices matter; smaller models on 8-bit quant can improve throughput at some accuracy tradeoff. we'll include model variants in the bench matrix.
03:58 Maria: are there specific kernels or infra tech you use? we've seen other vendors mention custom kernels and kv cache optimizations — we need to know what is out-of-the-box vs needs tuning.
04:12 Priya: redwood runtime picks kernels based on model arch and sequence length; some ops are fused on certain hw. kv cache is managed by the runtime and supports sticky sessions for long conversations, the bench will capture prefix cache hit/miss. sometimes transcriptions show 'K-V cash' in autogenerated notes, ignore that :)
04:34 Jordan: hah, yeah i've seen weird transcribes. ok on acceptance criteria — i want two things: functional parity with our current rule-based assistant (>=0.95 intent extraction accuracy) and infrastructure SLOs: p95 under 120ms for short prompts, and p99 under 350ms for 256 token requests under normal load. if bench shows better, great.
04:58 Alex: good concrete asks. we'll map those to pass/fail for the POC. any data residency constraints?
05:06 Tanya: european customer data must remain in eu, default is azure-west-europe. some telemetry can be aggregated outside but raw utterances must stay in-region.
05:18 Priya: that's doable; we'll run region-specific runs and also evaluate cross-region failover behavior.
05:26 Maria: what about encryption keys, we use Azure Key Vault and require BYOK (bring your own key) for production. we might accept a managed KMS for pilot if that's faster.
05:36 Alex: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and BYOK patterns on private/dedicated; hosted also supports customer-managed keys in some regions, but we'll need to confirm azure-kv specifically — action item for tanya to list exact requirements.
05:55 Jordan: what are the cost buckets you plan to show? i want per-token cost, cost per 1k QPS-hour, and monthly projected spend for 0.5x/1x/2x baselines.
06:09 Alex: yes we'll show per-token, per-embedding where relevant, and amortized reserved vs burst costs. we'll produce illustrative monthly burn tables.
06:20 Priya: benchmark design note: for marketing spikes we should simulate ramp to 5x over 90 seconds and sustain 12 minutes, that will stress autoscaling and cache warm-ups; it's important to observe tail behavior during those transients.
06:38 Maria: do you support canary/traffic splitting? our rollout plan uses 5% canary for a week, then ramp.
06:45 Alex: yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, model pinning and automatic fallback policies. we'll include rollout steps in the handoff doc.
06:55 Jordan: any blockers around compliance docs? we need SOC2 Type II, encryption at rest, SSO via SAML.
07:03 Alex: we have SOC2 docs and an enterprise pack, we can share a redacted cert and our security whitepaper; SE will coordinate to forward the specific KMS and network diagrams.
07:14 Tanya: last question on observability — do you expose per-token cost and latency per route - we need integration to our tracing and to show token-level cost in our dashboards.
07:26 Priya: yes, console has token-level breakdowns and tracing hooks; logs can be shipped to your SIEM and we have per-route dashboards. there might be small mapping work for your telemetry schema.
07:40 Jordan: ok, what are the acceptance steps at POC end — is it a pass/fail matrix?
07:47 Alex: we'll create a simple rubric: functional accuracy, latency SLOs, security checklist, and operational handoff. each item gets pass/warn/fail and a remediation plan. if all pass/warn then we consider the pilot successful and propose next phase (pilot -> dedicated procurement).
07:58 Maria: timeline wise, if we start now, bench results by 8/5, review week of 8/9, security deep-dive immediately after, procurement decision by late august? that's optimistic but feasible.
08:12 Alex: sounds reasonable. to recap next steps — priya does benches, alex sends pricing, luminary shares sample prompts and telemetry, tanya confirms compliance list. schedule follow-up for 8/10 (tentative).
08:30 Jordan: perfect, thanks everyone.
08:34 Alex: thanks all. action item recap will be in the notes.
